_comment: Critical-mutant manifest for tools/mutants.py (issue #18/#19, 'curl-style' assurance). Each entry BREAKS one security/correctness invariant by a precise reversible source transform; the named killer hosted test, after PASSING clean on pristine source (the baseline preflight), MUST then fail under the mutation (the mutant is KILLED). A SURVIVED mutant = the clean-passing test does not actually prove its invariant (a test defect). A BLOCKED mutant = an untrustworthy verdict: the killer did not pass on pristine source, the `find` pattern does not match exactly once (source drift), the mutated source failed to build (a compile failure is NEVER a kill), a timeout on a non-liveness mutant, or any infrastructure failure. Production code carries NO mutation macros; mutants live entirely here + in tools/mutants.py and every build/run happens in a private disposable snapshot, so the kernel source and the caller's worktree stay untouched. Keep the ENABLED set small and canonical (regression anchors whose killer test exists AND passes clean today). The DISABLED entries at the end are test-GAP markers: critical invariants whose killer test does NOT exist yet; they are enabled:false so `make mutants` stays green while documenting the missing coverage; enable each one when its killer test lands (and remove the placeholder find-string). Writing a deleter mutant as `if (0 && (<cond>))` keeps a variable used so -Werror does not turn a test gap into a spurious build failure. See docs/audit/2026-11-code-audit.md and docs/audit/2026-11-fix-gate.md (F01/F04) for provenance; AI-assisted, not human qualification.

mutants.invariant: je_pages_free rejects an out-of-window physical address BEFORE deriving a page index (prevents an OOB state[] write)
mutants.killer: test_physmem_arm: out-of-window / window-crossing free rejection

mutants.invariant: je_pages_init_pred is default-DENY: a page the predicate does not approve is RESERVED (the PR-H .bss-zero=ALLOW defect class)
mutants.killer: test_physmem: init state[] vs independent byte-level reference; exhaustion excludes reserved frames

mutants.invariant: resolve_slot denies a lookup whose handle lacks the required rights (a handle never grants more than it holds)
mutants.killer: test_handle: lookup with insufficient rights is DENIED

mutants.invariant: je_handle_duplicate can only REMOVE rights: a dup requesting rights not held by the source is DENIED (no privilege escalation by duplication)
mutants.killer: test_handle: duplicate requesting a superset of rights is DENIED

mutants.invariant: je_vm_image_validate rejects a descriptor whose segments overlap (or collide with the stack/guard) at page granularity
mutants.find: if (used[p]) return JE_ERR_INVALID; /* overlap or stack/guard */
mutants.replace: if (0 && (used[p])) return JE_ERR_INVALID; /* overlap or stack/guard */
mutants.killer: test_vm: overlapping-segment descriptor is rejected

mutants.invariant: je_fdt_parse rejects a blob whose magic is not JE_FDT_MAGIC (an untrusted non-DTB blob is never parsed as a DTB)
mutants.killer: test_fdt: bad-magic blob is rejected (JE_FDT_BAD_MAGIC)

mutants.invariant: je_sched_reap_dead reports a je_sched_drop_user failure as a NEGATIVE je_status, so the idle loop's `< 0` fail-stop guard fires instead of the error being miscounted as reaped slots (fix-gate F03)
mutants.killer: test_sched_killall: test_reap_drop_failure (page_restore -> JE_ERR_IO returns exactly -6; slot/PROCESS still DYING; no destroy)

mutants.invariant: je_sched_reap_dead with interrupts enabled is a fail-stop misuse: the liveness guards and destroy must be atomic vs a timer dispatch (fix-gate F03)
mutants.killer: test_sched_killall: test_reap_if_enabled_fail_stop (IF=1 -> abort_scheduler caught via longjmp; no destroy; slot still DYING)

mutants.invariant: je_sched_reap_dead never reaps a DYING slot whose address space is still the active CR3 (fix-gate F03)
mutants.killer: test_sched_killall: test_reap_active_cr3 (root == active CR3 -> -5, no page_restore/destroy, slot unchanged) and test_reap_partial_progress

mutants.invariant: je_sched_reap_dead never reaps a DYING slot whose kernel stack is still the live TSS.RSP0 (fix-gate F03)
mutants.killer: test_sched_killall: test_reap_active_rsp0 (rsp0_top == active TSS.RSP0 -> -5, no page_restore/destroy/waiter release, slot/PROCESS/registry unchanged)

mutants.invariant: je_sched_reap_dead tears down the slot's RECORDED vm_index (threads[i].vm_index), not the loop slot number (fix-gate F03)
mutants.killer: test_sched_killall: test_reap_partial_progress, test_reap_success_counts and the reaping sub-case of test_reap_active_cr3/rsp0, whose DYING slots use vm_index 8-slot (slot!=vm_index): exact destroy (vm, vm_index, owner) args and per-vm_index registry checks

mutants.invariant: a nonzero-length user copy rejects a NULL kernel buffer before scheduler and copy-run side effects
mutants.killer: test_usercopy: case C — NULL kernel buffer is invalid without scheduler or run side effects

mutants.invariant: a validated copy refuses nesting while preserving the active outer copy scope
mutants.find: if (g_scope.active) return JE_ABI_INVALID;   /* no nesting; outer scope intact */
mutants.replace: if (0 && g_scope.active) return JE_ABI_INVALID;   /* no nesting; outer scope intact */
mutants.killer: test_usercopy: case I — nested copy is invalid and the outer fixup scope remains active

mutants.invariant: a copy to user requires every covered page to have JE_VM_PERM_RW_NX
mutants.find: if (perm != JE_VM_PERM_RW_NX) return 0;  /* only RW/NX is writable */
mutants.replace: if (0 && (perm != JE_VM_PERM_RW_NX)) return 0;  /* only RW/NX is writable */
mutants.killer: test_usercopy: case F — writes to RX and R/NX pages are rejected

mutants.invariant: je_builtin_images_init publishes the registry (count/get) only after EVERY entry validates: a length mismatch on the last entry, after all earlier entries were staged, leaves nothing published and a retry still fails (fix-gate F10)
mutants.killer: test_image_registry_len_mismatch: broker-client blob_len 1 byte short of source_size -> JE_ERR_INVALID, count 0, get NULL, retry still INVALID

mutants.invariant: the supervisor built-in image is rejected unless exactly one RW non-X segment holds the fixed service report (Stage 2 report hook; fix-gate F10)
mutants.killer: test_image_registry_report_missing: code-only supervisor descriptor (vm_image_validate OK) -> JE_ERR_INVALID, nothing published

mutants.invariant: je_builtin_images_init rejects an empty or inverted spawn-child linker span (uintptr_t compare; fix-gate F10)
mutants.killer: test_image_registry_span_equal (end == start -> JE_ERR_INVALID, nothing published); test_image_registry_span_inverted checks end < start but cannot be named here (one run per entry)
mutants.equivalent_reason: Defense-in-depth guard, observationally subsumed today by je_vm_image_validate on the synthesized spawn-child descriptor: e == s gives source_size 0 so entry_offset 0 lies in no RX source byte (entry check fails); e < s wraps length past memory_size (source_size > memory_size fails). Either way init returns JE_ERR_INVALID and publishes nothing, so no hosted test can distinguish the deletion (verified 2026-11-08: span_equal and span_inverted both PASS under this mutant). Declared EQUIVALENT as a tripwire: if the validator or the synthesized descriptor changes so the guard becomes load-bearing, this killer FAILS under the mutant and the runner reports SURVIVED-as-declared-equivalent; then drop equivalent and keep it as a normal KILL anchor.

mutants.invariant: the recv kernel staging capacity handed to the endpoint peek is min(user cap, sizeof staging): a user cap never states a kernel buffer larger than JE_EP_MSG_MAX (fix-gate F10, defensive)
mutants.killer: test_syscall: test_recv_staging_cap (caps > JE_EP_MSG_MAX incl. UINT64_MAX clamp to JE_EP_MSG_MAX; helper only, the two dispatch call sites are QEMU-covered)

mutants.invariant: je_thread_create_user_start explicitly rejects a second THREAD_USER for a (vm,index) that already has one, BEFORE allocating a slot, re-guarding the held kstack, rewriting its frame, or (on a proc_link failure) page_restore-ing the first thread's guard page (fix-gate F08)
mutants.killer: test_sched_killall: test_create_user_one_thread_per_process (duplicate create on a REGISTERED and an UNREGISTERED (vm,index) -> JE_ERR_INVALID with no slot consumed, no second page_guard, no page_restore, threads/proc/registry/kstack bytes unchanged; different index and different vm still create)

mutants.invariant: je_endpoint_resolve returns the handle table's BADINDEX/STALE/WRONGTYPE verdict BEFORE object_to_end runs, so no malformed, not-live or wrong-type user handle reaches the INTERNAL JE_EP_CORRUPT that the F07 syscall glue routes to fail-stop (fix-gate F07; the glue routing itself is not hosted)
mutants.find:
if (s != JE_HANDLE_OK) return hstat(s);
    return object_to_end(pool, obj, out_rec, out_side);
mutants.replace:
if (0 && (s != JE_HANDLE_OK)) return hstat(s);
    return object_to_end(pool, obj, out_rec, out_side);
mutants.killer: test_endpoint: test_f07_resolve_precedence (zero/out-of-capacity -> BADINDEX, wrong-gen/closed -> STALE, SELF incl. SELF bound to a real end -> WRONGTYPE, each never CORRUPT/UNWIRED and with no out-param or accounting change). NOTE: in main() order the FIRST abort under this mutant is the pre-existing section 2 STALE double-close assertion; test_f07_resolve_precedence was separately verified (scratch copy, called first) to kill it on its own

mutants.invariant: je_vm_audit rejects a page table where two arena offsets map the same physical frame (no user-visible aliasing of a single frame)
mutants.killer: test_vm: test_audit_rejects_one_to_one_alias replaces an existing present leaf with a same-extent frame and restores it

mutants.invariant: wait_register pins the endpoint record with an inflight ref so a parked waiter's record cannot be freed while it sleeps (no use-after-free in the timeout sweep)
mutants.killer: GAP: peer audit's probe dropped the inflight ref and the mutant SURVIVED (close both handles while a thread is parked -> record freed under the sleeper). Add the killer test, pin the exact find-string, then enable.

mutants.invariant: je_device_apply_dispatch grants ring-3 port I/O only to the device's owner (identity, not merely active)
mutants.find: allow = d && d->owner.index == id.index && d->owner.gen == id.gen
mutants.killer: test_device: test_dispatch_authority owner/non-owner/gen-zero/kernel/revoked/inactive dispatch checks

mutants.invariant: the AArch64 audit's phase-1 structural walk rejects a valid table descriptor whose child frame is not a ledger member (FOREIGN) — including a late, off-path sibling like root[511] — so no unvalidated table frame is ever accepted or later read
mutants.killer: test_paging_bits test_structural_tampers case 1: root[511] / L2[200] -> mmap(PROT_NONE) page and root[511] -> in-window non-ledger frame must be INVALID with reason FOREIGN (and exactly 512 reads for root[511]); under the mutant the foreign entry is silently skipped and the audit returns JE_OK. Replaces the disabled GAP-ARM-AUDIT-FOREIGN-SIBLING marker (fix-gate F04). Written as a `continue` substitution, not `if (0 && ...)`: disabling the table_ordinal() call would leave child_ordinal uninitialized (a -Werror build failure = BLOCKED, or UB).

mutants.invariant: the AArch64 audit's phase-1 visited bitmap rejects any table reached twice (self-cycle, ancestor cycle, shared/repeated child) with reason REVISIT
mutants.killer: test_paging_bits test_structural_tampers cases 3-5: root[300]->root, L2[100]->L1, L1[5]->root, root[7]==root[0] must reject with reason REVISIT; under the mutant the walk re-enqueues until the work-list bound (COUNT) or over-counts visits (UNREACHED), so the exact-reason assertion fails

mutants.invariant: the AArch64 audit's phase 0 bounds table_count to [1, JE_ARM_MAX_TABLES] BEFORE indexing table_pa[] (no over-read on a corrupt count)
mutants.killer: test_paging_bits test_structural_tampers case 6: table_count 0 / MAX+1 / SIZE_MAX must reject with reason COUNT and zero descriptor reads; under the mutant 0 falls through to ROOT and MAX+1/SIZE_MAX index table_pa[] and hit LEDGER, failing the exact-reason assertion

mutants.invariant: je_arm_mmu_audit revokes the enable eligibility stamp (je_arm_last_audited) unconditionally on entry (C4), so ANY failed audit call — a failed re-audit of a previously-passing context, or even audit(NULL) — forbids je_arm_mmu_enable
mutants.killer: test_paging_bits struct_rejects (every structural case: OK audit, tamper, INVALID audit, then je_arm_mmu_enable must be JE_ERR_INVALID with the asm leaf never called) and test_enable_gating (OK audit, then audit(NULL) == INVALID/PRECONDITION, then enable must be INVALID with leaf_rec.calls == 0); under the mutant the stale stamp lets enable succeed. Find re-pinned after C4 made the clear unconditional (the old conditional find no longer exists).

mutants.invariant: the AArch64 audit's phase 0 rejects (LEDGER) any ledger table_pa[i] outside [table_start, table_end) BEFORE any table dereference (C2), so a coupled ledger tamper that moves an entry to an aligned, unique, below-2^44 foreign frame is never walked
mutants.killer: test_paging_bits test_structural_tampers case 8a (orphan just past table_end must be LEDGER with 0 reads; mutant -> UNREACHED) and case 8d (table_pa[5] / table_pa[0] moved to a PROT_NONE frame BASE+32*PG outside the window, no descriptor changed, must be LEDGER with 0 reads; mutant -> FOREIGN / ROOT)

mutants.invariant: the AArch64 audit's phase-2 alias scan rejects (ALIAS) a physical frame reachable via both an executable and a writable leaf, checked when the FIRST (valid, identity) leaf of the pair is reached. NOTE: under the identity (VA==PA) contract any cross-leaf alias also implies a non-identity leaf, so without the scan the audit still returns JE_ERR_INVALID (reason LEAF) when it reaches the second leaf; this mutant is killed by the exact-reason assertion, i.e. it proves the scan is reachable and classifies correctly, NOT that it is the sole barrier to an accepted alias
mutants.killer: test_paging_bits test_structural_tampers case 8e: a LATER RW data leaf (RODATA_HI) retargeted to the earlier text frame, and a LATER RX text leaf retargeted to the earlier table frame (BASE), must reject with reason ALIAS; under the mutant the earlier valid leaf passes and the tampered later leaf is rejected as LEAF (va != physical), failing the exact-reason assertion

mutants.invariant: the round-robin cursor advances to the selected READY slot, so a second READY worker is selected after the first instead of repeatedly selecting the first slot
mutants.killer: test_sched_rr: test_rr_order cycles idle -> A -> B -> A -> B

mutants.invariant: je_rr_pick excludes ZOMBIE slots from the READY candidate set
mutants.killer: test_sched_rr: test_zombie_exclusion exits A before the first pick and requires B, never A

mutants.invariant: je_rr_switch must reject a frame-check failure before dispatch and must never return an unvalidated resume frame
mutants.killer: test_sched_rr: test_frame_check_rejection rejects out-of-bounds and swapped fake frames with no returned frame

mutants.invariant: je_rr_switch changes the previous context to READY only when it was RUNNING, never resurrecting a SLEEPING or ZOMBIE context
mutants.killer: test_sched_rr: test_resurrect_guard keeps exited A ZOMBIE and sleeping B SLEEPING after switches/tick

mutants.invariant: je_lc_on_dying must propagate a je_proc_on_dying failure (not swallow it) so the run-queue caller fail-stops instead of publishing an inconsistent dying slot (ADR 0014)
mutants.killer: test_proc_lifecycle: test_on_dying_failure_propagates asserts an invalid reason makes je_lc_on_dying return non-OK

mutants.invariant: je_lc_on_dying must run the device dying hook while the PROCESS record is still LIVE, before je_proc_on_dying transitions it (ordering pinned by the neutral conformance suite; ADR 0014)
mutants.killer: test_proc_lifecycle: test_on_dying_fault asserts the record is LIVE when the device-dying hook runs

mutants.invariant: the MP3a-1 proof decorates every kernel-root L0 entry before process roots are built, so kernel mappings remain EL0-denied
mutants.killer: user-test audit-p1: an undecorated kernel root must be rejected before the process root is published

mutants.invariant: the p2 proof installs p2's own process root, not p1's root
mutants.killer: user-test TTBR0/root and cross-process isolation checks: p2 must read back its distinct root and frame

mutants.invariant: the per-process audit rejects any valid arena-branch L1 entry outside L1[0]
mutants.killer: user-test audit-p1: arena upper-entry emptiness must reject a stray L1[1] table

mutants.invariant: the per-process audit requires the guard hole and the stack's exact declared top-page placement
mutants.killer: user-test audit-p1: guard-page invalidity and exact stack-leaf placement must reject a shifted stack

mutants.invariant: the user-test oracle verifies kernel probe VAs against ELF symbols instead of accepting an arbitrary translation fault
mutants.find:
const uint64_t kernel_text = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)_text;
    const uint64_t kernel_data = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&je_arm_bss_probe;
mutants.replace:
const uint64_t kernel_text = UINT64_C(0x1000);
    const uint64_t kernel_data = UINT64_C(0x2000);
mutants.killer: smoke user-test ELF-VA and exact level-3 permission-fault checks: unmapped 0x1000/0x2000 probes must fail

mutants.invariant: the scheduler proof path emits the required ASIDE1IS invalidation for the installed ASID
mutants.killer: smoke user-test ELF instruction proof: the install seam must contain ASIDE1IS x1

mutants.invariant: TTBR0_EL1 installation includes the bounded 8-bit ASID selected by the proof
mutants.killer: user-test TTBR0 readback: both installs must retain ASID 1 in bits [55:48]

mutants.invariant: publishing a USER_CODE frame records it in the paging W^X ledger before a later RW alias can be attempted
mutants.killer: user-test W^X in-proof assertion: RW alias of p1 USER_CODE must return JE_ERR_DENIED
